editorial: When the jungle drums begin to beat, you’re thrust into 1971’s brutal border skirmishes in Border 2 (2026). Three idealistic soldiers from the army, navy and air force show how camaraderie can transcend service branches, offering a fresh perspective in a familiar war drama setting. The air force lieutenant’s silent diversion, filmed through a claustrophobic tunnel, turns a tense operation into a visceral chase that grips you. At times the pacing jerks as the film lulls to long static shots before the climax, slightly diluting urgency. Ideal for fans of historical war dramas who crave raw, character-driven realism.
